title: The Season That Changed the Conversation Around Mumbai Indians
dek: Some seasons change how a franchise is talked about. For Mumbai Indians, the biggest swing in results came in 2010.
excerpt: In 2010, Mumbai Indians' win rate jumped further from the previous season than in any other year. That is the season most likely to have changed the conversation about them.

sections.heading: Measuring a Change in the Conversation
body: Narratives about a team shift when results shift sharply. The clearest measurable signal is the largest change in win rate from one season to the next.
For Mumbai Indians, that came in {{ev:sc-year}}: their win rate went from {{ev:sc-from}} to {{ev:sc-to}}. The chart shows every season.

A jump this large usually reflects new players, a new captain or a new plan, rather than luck alone.

sections.heading: Why This Season Matters
body: A swing season resets expectations. Fans, rivals and the franchise itself measure later seasons against it.

sections.heading: Swings Are Partly Noise
body: Season win rates come from around fourteen to sixteen matches, so part of any swing is chance. Large swings are still more likely than small ones to reflect real change.
The other history articles in this series look at what changed on the field in Mumbai Indians' best seasons.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: 2010 Reset the Story
body: 2010 is the season in which Mumbai Indians' results changed most. It is the natural starting point for any account of how the franchise is now seen.
Whether it actually changed the public conversation needs media data to confirm.
